title: Greenfield Go library: word frequency counter with top-N and stop-words
description: Build a Go library from scratch that counts word frequencies with stop-word filtering and top-N retrieval.

task_spec.prompt:
Create a Go library in wordfreq/wordfreq.go (package wordfreq) with:

type Counter struct { ... }  // holds word counts

func New(stopWords []string) *Counter
  Creates a new Counter. Words in stopWords are ignored during counting (case-insensitive).

func (c *Counter) Add(text string)
  Tokenizes text (split on whitespace, strip punctuation, lowercase) and increments counts, skipping stop words.

func (c *Counter) Count(word string) int
  Returns the count for word (case-insensitive). Returns 0 if not seen.

func (c *Counter) TopN(n int) []struct{ Word string; Count int }
  Returns the top n words by count, highest first. Ties broken alphabetically. Returns empty slice if n <= 0.

Write 8+ tests in wordfreq/wordfreq_test.go covering:
  basic counting, stop-word filtering, punctuation stripping, TopN basic, TopN with ties, TopN n=0 returns empty, Count for unseen word returns 0, case-insensitive matching.

go test ./... and go build ./... must pass.
required_artifacts: wordfreq/wordfreq.go with Counter struct and New/Add/Count/TopN
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
